title: Best Trampolines for Kids UK
short: Garden and toddler trampolines compared for safety features, bounce quality and durability, tested by parents and checked against RoSPA safety guidance.
intro: A trampoline's safety features and build quality matter more than bounce height alone, especially after months of year-round British weather. This guide compares trampolines tested by Mumsnet's parent testers with their own children, judged on assembly, safety features, bounce performance and durability, and checked against Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents guidance.

products.name: Space Zone II Trampoline
products.best_for: Families who want the best balance of safety, durability and value
products.key_spec: 8ft-14ft sizes, Springsafe 3G enclosure, galvanised steel frame, max user weight 75-125kg
products.summary: Tested by mum of two Maddie, whose sons have used it heavily for three years and it still looks almost new. The Springsafe 3G enclosure keeps jumpers separated from springs and frame, and assembly proved straightforward, with Maddie's partner building it solo in two hours despite Plum recommending two people, though the ladder is sold separately.
pros: Springs safely enclosed away from bounce mat
Weatherproof, rust-resistant galvanised frame
Relatively quick, straightforward assembly
Held up to three years of heavy daily use in testing
cons: Ladder sold separately
Minor spare parts can be hard to source

products.name: 8ft Wave Springsafe Trampoline
products.best_for: Families who want a safe, sturdy trampoline without a large footprint or price
products.key_spec: 8ft, Springsafe 2G enclosure, galvanised steel frame, max user weight 50kg
products.summary: Tested by Mumsnet editor and mum of three Jenny, who found it felt stable and sturdy without wobbling, with her children using it for everything from a stage to a rocket ship. The 2G Springsafe enclosure and weather-protected foam pads add real reassurance for younger children, though assembly takes just under two hours and is easier with two people.
pros: Excellent value for the safety features included
Compact footprint suits smaller gardens
Weather-resistant, galvanised steel frame
Felt stable and sturdy in testing
cons: Time-consuming to assemble
50kg weight limit suits younger children only

products.name: Ultima 4 10ft Trampoline
products.best_for: Families who want a premium-feeling trampoline in a mid-size footprint
products.key_spec: 10ft, weldless frame, 20mm foam padding, smart folding net, max user weight 120kg
products.summary: Mumsnet found this feels more premium than many similarly sized models, with a patented weldless frame designed for strength and a high 120kg weight capacity suiting older children, teens and even adults. A standout smart folding net lowers or raises in around five minutes without tools, though assembly is very much a two-person job.
pros: High 120kg weight capacity suits older children and adults
Smart folding net for quick protection after use
Thick 20mm foam padding
Sold with ladder included
cons: Best suited to experienced bouncers
Two-person assembly that can take a while

products.name: Up 10ft Trampoline
products.best_for: Families with plenty of garden space who want strong value
products.key_spec: 10ft (also available 12ft), IGLOO zip-free door, galvanised steel frame, max user weight 100kg
products.summary: Mumsnet found this combines plenty of bouncing space with strong safety credentials and very good value, with a patented zip-free IGLOO door removing the usual worries of snagged clothing. The galvanised steel frame felt sturdy and stable in testing, and it's used by Olympic gold medallist Bryony Page, though tying the protective net to the base can be fiddly.
pros: Zip-free IGLOO door design reduces snagging and wear
Sturdy galvanised steel frame
Good value for a large trampoline
Also available in a larger 12ft size
cons: Netting can be fiddly to attach during assembly
Takes around two hours to assemble
Only suitable from age six

products.name: Junior Bouncer
products.best_for: Toddlers and preschoolers taking their first bounces
products.key_spec: 18 months+, spring-free elastic cord design, soft-grip handle, max user weight 25kg
products.summary: Tested by Mumsnet's Deputy Head of Content and toddler mum Laura, whose 19-month-old loves it and feels confident getting on and off independently. The spring-free design uses woven elastic cords for a softer, gentler bounce than metal springs, and Laura found it felt exceptionally stable, though assembly took around 45 minutes and it doesn't fold for storage.
pros: Spring-free design gives a gentler, safer bounce
Easy for toddlers to get on and off independently
Excellent grip handle for small hands
Stable on different surfaces
cons: Doesn't fold for storage
Bright design won't suit every home
Wide footprint can be awkward in small spaces

products.name: Toddler Trampoline
products.best_for: Introducing very young children to bouncing on a budget
products.key_spec: 18 months+, padded frame cover, non-slip feet, max user weight 20kg
products.summary: Mumsnet found this a reassuringly simple option for introducing trampolining, with a padded frame cover, non-slip feet and a sturdy foam-grip handle to help toddlers stay balanced. It's lightweight, compact and easy to move indoors or outside, though the 20kg weight limit means children will outgrow it fairly quickly.
pros: Affordable first trampoline
Comes with a padded safety mat
Suitable for indoor or outdoor use
Lightweight and easy to move
cons: Children outgrow the 20kg limit quickly
Much smaller and more basic than premium toddler models

products.name: Nursery Trampoline
products.best_for: Parents who want a compact trampoline usable indoors or out
products.key_spec: 12 months-3 years, detachable handle and legs, 4kg, max user weight 20kg
products.summary: Mumsnet found this well-designed for young children, with detachable handle and legs making it easy to store and highly portable at just 4kg for use indoors or outside. It includes a handlebar for stability and padded frame cover, in playful turtle or unicorn designs, though some found it tricky to assemble and pricey for a small trampoline.
pros: Detachable parts make storage easy
Very portable at just 4kg
Usable indoors or outdoors
Padded frame cover and stability handlebar
cons: Some find assembly tricky, needs two people
Pricey for a small trampoline
20kg weight limit suits younger toddlers only

products.name: Sport-Pro Trampoline
products.best_for: Children practising tricks who want an even bounce across the whole mat
products.key_spec: 8 x 10ft rectangular, Quad Lok frame system, galvanised steel, max user weight 100kg
products.summary: Mumsnet found the rectangular shape gives a more even bounce across the whole mat than round trampolines, thanks to strong zinc-coated springs and a durable jump mat, making it good for children practising skills. It fits neatly in many UK gardens without dominating the space, though it's not suitable for under-sixes and takes around two hours to assemble.
pros: Even, consistent bounce across the full mat
Fits neatly in gardens where round trampolines feel intrusive
Strong, rust-resistant galvanised frame
Extra thick outer padding
cons: Not suitable for children under six
Two-person assembly taking around two hours

products.name: Oval Combo Pro Trampoline
products.best_for: Families with children of different ages who want maximum bounce space
products.key_spec: 10 x 15ft oval, welded-socket T-connector frame, ladder and tie-down kit included, max user weight 120kg
products.summary: Mumsnet found this large, high-capacity model gives plenty of room for children, teens and even adults to bounce comfortably, with a more controlled bounce than a rectangular alternative. It comes as a complete package with ladder, tie-down kit and protective spring padding, though it needs significant garden space and takes time to assemble.
pros: Spacious oval frame suits children, teens and adults
Controlled, even bounce
Comes complete with ladder and tie-down kit
Sturdy welded-socket frame built for long-term use
cons: Expensive
Needs a large amount of garden space
Two-person assembly that takes time

guide.q: What size trampoline should I buy?
guide.a: Choose the largest model that fits your garden while still leaving the manufacturer's required safety clearance, since a bigger trampoline like the 10ft or 12ft models here gives children more room to grow into. An 8ft trampoline like the Plum Wave here is the most popular size among Mumsnet parents and suits smaller gardens well.

guide.q: Round, rectangular or oval: which shape is best?
guide.a: Round trampolines are the most common and give a gentle bounce that naturally pulls jumpers back towards the centre. A rectangular trampoline like the Sportspower here gives a more even bounce across the whole mat, favoured by budding gymnasts, while an oval like the JumpKing here combines a generous jumping area with a more controlled bounce than rectangular models.

guide.q: What safety features should I look for?
guide.a: RoSPA guidance highlights padded spring and frame covers, a safety enclosure net, and ground anchors to secure the trampoline in high winds. Look for a trampoline tested to the current domestic safety standard, BS EN 71-14:2025, and always supervise children and enforce one-jumper-at-a-time to avoid collision injuries.

guide.q: Can I leave a trampoline outside over winter?
guide.a: Yes, most trampolines are robust enough to stay outdoors year-round, but it's worth covering them with a weatherproof cover to protect against rain, frost and snow. If the trampoline feels light, use an anchor kit to stop it moving in storms, or dismantle and store it in a shed or garage for maximum protection.
